title: Recently came across an AI market prediction tool.
author: Parking_911_turbo
selftext:
Pardon my language but recently I came across an market prediction tool. A friend told me about this but I have always been skeptical about using any such tools as I've seen jokers dancing on prediction failing miserably.

I was introduced to this tool as a stock market learning game by a friend. It basically gives you a confidence score on the predicted market movements, gives are news articls and reasons why the market might move. basically wont make a descion for you but gives the info that you need to make that decision and allows you to mock buy stocks.

Now the interesting and the part im curious about, I noticed a pattern where the confidence score were high for a few shared and the predictions were approximate, not very off. used the game data to buy real shares and it seemed to work.

But now I'm worried as I have lost a decent amount while starting trading when i had no clue about how market works and took advices from 'Experts' who predicted..

Intially I got all returns, but eventually I lost some goof amount of money before I started to learn and trade by myself. I dont want to get used to the prediction tool for my decisions even though it makes my work easier.

I wanted to know if anyone had such experiecned? how reliable are these tools?

comments.author: Due_Set_6523
comments.body: a high confidence score isn’t a probability of profit, and mock trades skip the hard parts ( fees, slippage and your own emotions). a few good calls also isn’t a track record. check how it holds up across rougher market stretches before trusting the pattern.

replies.author: Parking_911_turbo
replies.body: Thats exactly what im worried about. Currently mapping out the predictions, but deep inside, i feel I can never completely trust this. I always have this fear that until you put in a large amount and gamble, its gonna be all positive outcomes, the moment you put all your stakes , it flips! So yeah, how much ever it gives me the right guesses, I'd still be skeptical unless someone who's already used one of these tells me how it works. I dont want to blindly trust a stockmartket imaginary god more than my research and instincts.

comments.author: DadsGamesandCharles
comments.body:
Not to salt your game but this sounds like a gotcha. If you put the name of this supposed tool in a comment on your post it would go much further. Right now it just sounds like for the low price of $15.99 we can DM you and find out what this is called.

Prediction things like this work but are only as reliable as the builder. I actually built a game and embedded a prediction engine in it (which is why this post caught my eye) and it worked good, but I would’ve probably had better results with a theoretical statistician quantum mechanical engineer.

We would’ve had so many good conversations and beers.

replies.author: Parking_911_turbo
replies.body:
Did not fully understand your comment, but I can ask the dude if Ican share the file here or share the link here. I doubt if he's made it public. Some dude had texted me asking the same.  
And the builders not been a great predictor of stock market movements, in fact he's given me some terrible market advices lol.  
But somehow, his app seems to be working better than him.

He's the 'stock market expert' I was referring to in the first comment.
